meta.title: GSB Seva Mandal Mahaganapati
meta.location: Shree Sukriteendra Nagar, A. Rama Nayak Hall and GSB Sports Club Ground, near SNDT Women's College, R. A. Kidwai Road, King's Circle, Matunga, Mumbai 400019
meta.foundedNote: The institution dates its Ganeshotsav to 1955. The parent charitable trust began in 1951; those are different events.
meta.intro: The King's Circle Mahaganapati is the annual festival of GSB Seva Mandal, a charitable organisation with roots in community service. Its five-day Ganeshotsav began in 1955 and retains a close association with Shri Kashi Math. Clay preparation, worship, collective meals and volunteer work provide a fuller archive than the widely circulated ornamented front view alone. This collection treats the festival venue in Matunga separately from the mandal's Sion office and from Wadala's independently organised GSB Ganeshotsav.

paragraphs.text: The trust traces its beginning to Vijaya Dashami in 1951, when GSB members working in Kamala Mills organised help with funerals and related rites. Weekly bhajans followed in a small Prabhadevi room. Its retrospective connects Madhav Puranik and the early volunteers with service at Walkeshwar Shri Kashi Math. These origins place the later public celebration within an existing network of mutual assistance.

Ganeshotsav began in 1955 under the blessings of Sudhindra Teertha, initially with a fourteen-inch idol. A community history records the move to Sukriteendra Nagar in 1971. The institution associates its 1979 silver jubilee with a silver crown and 1997 with a golden crown during a Chaturmas gathering. These are attributed landmarks, rather than independently authenticated inventories of historic ornaments.

Before making Mahaganapati, the mandal describes taking clay and a coconut for prayer at Madhavendra Teertha's Vrindavan at Walkeshwar Kashi Math. The coconut is then placed within the idol. The practice gives the making process a religious geography extending beyond the festival ground. The large garlanded, ornamented seated form in recent press photographs belongs to this annual temporary installation.

The 2026 appeal specifies five days, 14-18 September, and describes a volunteer-run setting of worship and shared service. Its wider work includes educational and medical assistance and an Annadaan initiative begun during the pandemic. The archive should preserve kitchens, seva organisation and material preparation alongside the deity, while keeping permanent premises, future projects and annual festival structures distinct.

sections.title: A physical festival across independently dated visits

paragraphs.text: Arun Shanbhag's 2009 visit explicitly separates King's Circle from the Wadala celebration and household worship. His account describes priests, repeated pujas and large-scale preparation of coconut-and-jaggery offerings. The attached King's Circle stage photograph retains both his copyright and the later Photobucket host overlay; neither is removed to make it look like an unaltered camera master.

His 2011 photograph has a useful provenance check: the current page's alt text mentions both 2011 and 2012, but the selected attachment title, attachment date and camera timestamp consistently support 2011. The separately published 2012 Tolay Bhaar account says the family ritual occurred during the preceding year, and its camera metadata also points to 2011. Publication and upload years therefore cannot create a new 2012 idol record.

Contemporary scenes from 2014,2015,2016,2017 and 2018 extend the visible silver-arch and ornamented-idol sequence with separate photographer or supplier credits. The sources identify King's Circle specifically; generic GSB wording is insufficient because several roundups also cover the independent Wadala institution. Exact daily capture times and unidentified artists remain open.

The 2022 unveiling report places the renewed public festival after a two-year interruption to ordinary participation, while the 2023 and 2026 frames are supported by current-event descriptions. These records do not establish the precise form or outcome of every pandemic-year ritual. Firoze Shakir's public collection lists an earlier annual sequence, but its album permission gate is respected and no unseen photographs are counted.

years.title: A four-foot idol and online darshan
years.summary: During the pandemic, GSB Seva Mandal installed a four-foot Ganesh at King's Circle after permission for its usual large idol was denied. Trustee RG Bhat told The Times of India that the idol carried no jewellery and that devotees could join by livestream.

claims.text: Trust foundation in 1951 and festival foundation in 1955 are distinct.
The venue move is dated 1971 in a community history.
Clay and coconut preparation are described by the mandal.
The 2026 notice specifies a five-day festival.
Both selected annual idol images have a physical festival setting and named press credits.
The selected Arun Shanbhag image is supported as 2011 by its original attachment title/date and camera metadata, despite mixed 2011/2012 current alt text.
claims.status: primary author and attachment metadata; not independent authentication

claims.text: Arun's Tolay Bhaar post published in 2012 describes the preceding year and cannot date its pictures to 2012.

researchNotes.coverage: Trust and festival histories, annual appeals, a community periodical and two inspected contemporary press photographs. This is the King's Circle annual event, not Wadala. Phase 2: 10 annual entries supplemented after direct image inspection; source labels and photographic appearance assessed separately.
gaps: No early 1955-2008 idol photographs obtained; some later years remain absent.
Pandemic 2020-2021 decisions, installed forms and eventual outcomes need institution-specific records; Wadala's postponement must not be transferred here.
Firoze Shakir's public index lists 2008-2015/2017/2019 albums but the tested album requires permission/sign-in. These are leads, not acquired photo years.
An official 2016 gallery route currently serves an unrelated 2026 appeal; its cached 2016 image is withheld until a stable dated archive capture is available.
The 2012 Tolay Bhaar post contains 2011 camera images; publication/upload folder is not a 2012 festival date.
A 2012 Rediff GSB photograph explicitly belongs to Ram Mandir Wadala and is assigned to that collection.
Individual historical makers and original reuse licences remain unverified.
